宏福苑獨立委員會聆訊披露，管理公司「置邦興業」曾編製一份名為「授權黃碧嬌的單位」的檔案，顯示在 2021 年 12 月 11 日選聘顧問「鴻毅」的業主大會上，有 131 張授權票與黃碧嬌團隊有關，佔當日整體授權票約 25%。《集誌社》取得授權記錄後發現，131 張授權票授權了連同黃碧嬌在內的 53 人；以該 53 人名單統計，當日黃碧嬌「友好」授權票多達 252 張，佔整體近五成。這個龐大的網絡有何背景？其中，有 5 人與太和邨舊法團委員同名同姓，該法團在 2016 年因天價工程爭議被推翻；部分太和邨舊法團委員在 2021 年 12 月亦「跨邨」現身宏福苑業主大會。翻查資料顯示，當年涉及太和邨維修爭議的顧問「浩熙」以低價中標，該公司曾參與宏福苑工程投標；而「浩熙」擔任大圍景田苑顧問時，工程由「宏業」中標，曾被業主入稟質疑圍標。記者透過短訊、電郵及區議員辦事處向黃碧嬌查詢，截稿前未獲回覆。相關報道：追查黃碧嬌授權票·2 ｜53 人取得 131 張授權票　他們是誰？　部分人具民建聯、新社聯等背景 追查黃碧嬌授權票·3 ｜兩名業主離世後　姓名出現「授權黃碧嬌單位」名單　家人不知情

The hearing revealed that Wang Fuk Court held an owners' meeting on 11 December 2021, with 131 proxy votes linked to the Wong Pik Kiu team. The agenda that day included the appointment of engineering consultant 'Hung Ngai' and a motion to remove the old owners' corporation. (Owners' corporation photo)

The hearing revealed that Wong Pik Kiu initially admitted to having collected only about 20 proxy votes, but the committee found a file named 'Units Authorising Wong Pik Kiu' in the records of the management company 'Hop On', which recorded that she had 131 proxy votes at the 2021 meeting, accounting for about 25% of the proxy votes that day. The majority of the 131 proxy votes were not issued to Wong as the proxy holder; she subsequently explained through her lawyer that the figure was a 'combined count' involving her volunteer team, incumbent owners' corporation members, community friends and others, totalling 131 'assisted handling' votes, while only about 20-plus explicitly authorised her personally.

The Collective obtained multiple sets of proxy vote records from Wang Fuk Court owners' meetings, including the lists from the 25 January 2019 meeting appointing 'Hung Ngai' as Registered Inspector (RI), the 11 December 2021 meeting appointing 'Hung Ngai' as consultant, the 28 January 2024 meeting appointing 'Wang Yip' as contractor, the 6 September 2024 meeting appointing a new owners' corporation, and the 'Units Authorising Wong Pik Kiu' file.

In December 2021, former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairperson Tam Lai Ha (left), treasurer Shek Yuk Chun (front centre), committee member Ng Ling Lan (back centre) and Mok Shuk Ching (right) showed up at the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting. That day, Mok Shuk Ching was seen holding a stack of papers, standing near the 'Proxy Registration Desk'. (Photo provided by interviewee)

Former Tai Wo Estate OC members involved in repair disputes showed up at Wang Fuk Court meeting

The 131 proxy votes at the December 2021 owners' meeting involved 129 owners, with 53 people as first proxy holders including Wong Pik Kiu. Among them, 'Tam Lai Ha', 'Shek Yuk Chun', 'Mok Shuk Ching', 'Yiu Kam Sheung' and 'Ng Ling Lan' each held 3 to 4 proxy votes, totalling 17 votes. These five people share the same names as former Tai Wo Estate OC committee members — Tam Lai Ha was former chairperson, Shek Yuk Chun was former treasurer, and the other three were former committee members.

Former Tai Wo Estate mutual aid committee member A (pseudonym), who had been following the repair and OC disputes, went to the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting venue in December 2021 to observe the situation. She recalled that upon arrival, she noticed several former Tai Wo Estate OC committee members, including Tam Lai Ha, Shek Yuk Chun, Mok Shuk Ching and Ng Ling Lan, present. 'I thought it was very strange, it was as if they were the hosts, the whole venue was Wong Pik Kiu doing the reception… one or two of them showing up wouldn't be odd, but a whole team came… my instinct was, is this related to you people again?' A provided photos from that day, pointing out that Mok Shuk Ching was holding a stack of papers beside the 'Proxy Registration Desk' at the time, constantly making phone calls while 'wandering around' and 'queuing to collect voting forms'.

Tai Wo Estate was embroiled in a sky-high construction bid-rigging scandal in 2016. The then OC eventually re-tendered, and the project cost dropped from HK$27 million to between HK$500,000 and HK$700,000. The OC was subsequently ousted.

Speaking about the Tai Wo Estate bid-rigging scandal, A said Tai Wo residents had approached the Housing Bureau's ICU, which oversaw the project, and learned that the government repair order only covered a small portion of the external wall area of buildings where concrete spalling had occurred. However, the OC decided, without consulting residents, to repair the entire external walls of three blocks, and lobbied residents by claiming the estate's maintenance fund had over HK$100 million and residents would not need to contribute. When residents sought to understand the decision, they were refused entry to meetings on the grounds that attendance was limited to five people.

Records show that the Tenants Purchase Scheme public housing estate Tai Wo Estate became embroiled in a sky-high repair scandal in 2016. Tam Lai Ha and Shek Yuk Chun were the then OC chairperson and treasurer, while Yiu Kam Sheung, Mok Shuk Ching and Ng Ling Lan were committee members. The OC at that time engaged consultant 'Ho Hei Construction Engineering Consultants' to conduct external wall inspections, with consultancy fees of about HK$150,000. Quotes for the external wall repair of three blocks reached as high as HK$27 million, with each household required to bear over HK$10,000. The project costs sparked a bid-rigging controversy. After residents lobbied, the project was re-tendered, and the cost was reduced to between HK$500,000 and HK$700,000. The old OC was ousted that same year.

Tam Lai Ha (seventh from left) ran in the 2003 District Council election under the DAB banner and lost, while serving as Tai Wo Estate OC chairperson from the early 2000s until being ousted in 2016. The photo shows a group picture at the 2015 Tai Po Rural Committee inauguration dinner, with Wong Pik Kiu second from left. (Facebook photo)

Former Tai Wo OC chairperson has DAB ties

Appearing on the 'Authorising Wong Pik Kiu' list and holding Wang Fuk Court proxy votes, former Tai Wo OC chairperson Tam Lai Ha has DAB background. She ran under the party in the 2003 Tai Po District Council election and lost, while her party colleague Wong Pik Kiu won. In 2006, Tam was appointed as an additional member of the Tai Po District Council Culture, Recreation and Sports Committee. During the September 2016 New Territories East by-election, she campaigned for DAB candidates Chan Hak Kan and Chow Ho Ting. Former committee member Mok Shuk Ching served alongside Wong Pik Kiu on the Tai Po District Fight Crime Committee in 2009, and became a specially invited director of the New Forum in 2021. Yiu Kam Sheung is also a New Forum Tai Po district director. As for Shek Yuk Chun and Ng Ling Lan, they are current members of the Tai Po Po Nga Area Care Team.

Besides the December 2021 owners' meeting appointing 'Hung Ngai', 'Shek Yuk Chun' and 'Ng Ling Lan' each received one proxy vote at the September 2024 owners' meeting appointing the new OC, with 'Wong Chun Yau' also listed as another proxy holder. Records show that 'Wong Chun Yau' co-founded the 'Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance' with Wong Pik Kiu.

The reporter contacted Wong Pik Kiu via text message, email and through a district councillor's office, but no reply was received before deadline.

Wong Pik Kiu founded the 'Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance' with Wong Chun Yau (left) and Ding Kit Mui (right). On the 'Units Authorising Wong Pik Kiu' list, there are proxy holders of the same name, as well as people sharing names with those connected to the 'Lok Kwan Volunteers'. (Facebook photo)

Tai Wo Estate consultant had bid for Wang Fuk Court; project at King Tin Court handled by 'Wang Yip' was awarded to 'Wang Yip'

The 'Ho Hei' consultancy that charged Tai Wo Estate a very low consultancy fee was founded by Wong Siu Cheung, who also bid for Wang Fuk Court projects. In January 2019, 'Ho Hei' bid HK$700,000 for the Wang Fuk Court Registered Inspector (RI) work, exceeding 'Hung Ngai's' HK$220,000 and failing to win the contract.

By 2021, 'Tai Tei Construction Consultants Limited', of which Wong Siu Cheung had been a director, bid HK$400,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy, slightly higher than 'Hung Ngai's' HK$300,000 and failing to win. 'Fai Lei Tat Construction Engineering Consultants Limited' bid HK$280,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy and likewise failed to win; Wong Siu Cheung became a director of 'Fai Lei Tat' the following year.

Court documents show that in 2009, Tai Wai King Tin Court engaged 'Ho Hei' as project consultant. After tendering in 2011, 'Wang Yip' was appointed as contractor for a HK$91 million project. In 2012, an owner filed a lawsuit alleging bid-rigging and seeking to have the contract set aside, but lost the case.

The 'Ho Hei' consultancy that won the Tai Wo Estate repair consultancy at a low price in 2016 subsequently bid for the Wang Fuk Court Registered Inspector work, and a related company also bid for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy — both bids exceeded Hung Ngai's and failed to win.

Wong Siu Cheung and Wong Siu Keung, who was previously involved in the Sha Tin Lakeview Garden bid-rigging case, are also suspected to be connected parties. During the trial of the Sha Tin Lakeview HK$260 million bid-rigging case, it was revealed that Wong Siu Cheung, a director of 'Universal Housing', paid 'tea money' and referral fees to OC members and project subcontractors, and arranged for shell companies to bid so that 'Universal Housing' would win the contract. In 2023, Wong Siu Cheung was arrested in connection with a HK$160 million bid-rigging case involving Discovery Bay. Company search records show that one of the dissolved construction companies of which Wong Siu Cheung had been a director shared the same registered address as that used by Wong Siu Keung.
